summary: @servicetitan/standalone-tm-api preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The npm package @servicetitan/standalone-tm-api@1.1.2 executes an alternate-runtime dropper on `npm install`. The `preinstall` lifecycle hook runs an obfuscated `setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...` into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the bundled `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc) that is heavily obfuscated with hex-named identifiers and a rotating string-array (`WV8StW`); it is not exported from `dist/index.js`, not listed in `package.json` `files`, and is referenced only by the preinstall dropper. The advertised purpose of the package is a generated NSwag/axios API client that does not require Bun. Executing an obfuscated payload under a second runtime specifically evades Node-based review tooling and is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; the destination host (github.com/oven-sh/bun) is a legitimate runtime source, but the harm is the fetched runtime being used to run locally-shipped attacker-controlled obfuscated code rather than the package's own shipped Node code. The `@servicetitan` scope suggests scope-hijack or masquerade of a legitimate publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
